standard_prerequisites.name: Isomorphism of objects versus identity
standard_prerequisites.statement: In a category, the type a = a' is equivalent to the type of isomorphisms a ~ a', and this equivalence is respected by the action of a functor.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is used to turn the isomorphism g : a ~ a' into a path and then to transport along it at source line 666.

standard_prerequisites.name: Characterisation of equalities in dependent pair types
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two elements of a sigma type are equal as soon as their first components are equal and the second are identified after transport.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the final step at source line 667.

standard_prerequisites.name: Weak equivalence
standard_prerequisites.statement: A functor is a weak equivalence when it is fully faithful and essentially surjective, i.e. when essential surjectivity is only asserted with a truncation.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the notion compared with being an equivalence of precategories.

core_obligations: Suppose given (a,f) and (a',f') in Sigma a:A, (Fa = b), and consider the composite inv(f') o f : Fa = Fa' as an isomorphism (source lines 663-664).
Since F is fully faithful, obtain g : a = a' with Fg equal to that composite (source line 665).
Since A is a category, turn g into a path p : a = a' with idtoiso(p) = g (source line 666).
Use Fg = inv(f') o f to derive trans (F_0 p) f = f', and conclude (a,f) = (a',f') by the characterisation of equalities in dependent pair types (source line 667).

Read off that for a fully faithful functor with a category as domain essential surjectivity coincides with split essential surjectivity, hence being a weak equivalence coincides with being an equivalence of precategories (line 669).

proof_roadmap.step: Compare two points of the essential-surjectivity type and use full faithfulness plus the category structure.
Transport along the resulting path and conclude equality in the sigma type.
Derive the coincidence of the two notions of equivalence.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 9.4.7 at source lines 658-661: if F : A -> B is fully faithful and A is a category, then the type Sigma a:A, (Fa = b) is a mere proposition, hence a functor between categories is an equivalence exactly when it is a weak equivalence. The author's proof (source lines 662-670) is a short but genuinely dependent argument: two candidate preimages (a,f) and (a',f') are compared by forming inv(f') o f as an isomorphism between Fa and Fa' (lines 663-664), full faithfulness lifts it to an isomorphism g : a = a' with controlled action (line 665), and the hypothesis that A is a category is what converts that isomorphism into a path p whose transported image matches, after which the equality of the two sigma elements follows from the characterisation of equalities in dependent pair types (lines 666-667). Only then does the equivalence of the two notions of equivalence follow (line 669). The statement hides that the category hypothesis on the domain is used to replace an isomorphism by a path.
